rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html lines 596-598 (equicorrelated normals are MTP2 for 0 <= rho < 1; one-sided p-values; the Simes step at line 598), Lab 5 hypothesis (line 638)
rows.evidence: Re-derived at d10fb51. (a) Sigma = (1-rho) I + rho 11' with Sherman-Morrison: Sigma^{-1} = (1/(1-rho)) [I - rho 11'/(1-rho+m0 rho)], so the off-diagonal entries of Q are -rho/((1-rho)(1-rho+m0 rho)) <= 0 for 0 <= rho < 1. (b) For a normal density with precision Q, log f(z) = const - (1/2) z'Qz; with u = x v y and v = x ^ y, u_i^2 + v_i^2 = x_i^2 + y_i^2, so the diagonal terms cancel and log f(u) + log f(v) - log f(x) - log f(y) = (1/2) sum_{i != j} Q_ij (x_i x_j + y_i y_j - u_i u_j - v_i v_j). The bracket is 0 when (x_i - y_i)(x_j - y_j) >= 0 and equals (x_i - y_i)(x_j - y_j) <= 0 otherwise (checked in the four sign cases), so each term Q_ij times the bracket is >= 0 and f(u) f(v) >= f(x) f(y). Numerical spot check (num/simes_mtp2_check.out): 200,000 random pairs for each of (m, rho) = (3, 0.2), (5, 0.7), (10, 0.95), (20, 0): min(lhs - rhs) = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, -1.4e-14 (rounding), violations 0. (c) One-sided p-values are decreasing in z coordinatewise, which swaps join and meet, and the Jacobian is a product of one-coordinate factors that cancels because {u_i, v_i} = {x_i, y_i}: the true-null p-values are MTP2 as the page says. PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html Proposition 7.8 and proof (lines 600-607)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 8352c53 (git diff checked); round-14 evidence: no round-9 change was recorded for this row (it carried the round-8 evidence below). round-8 evidence: Re-derived after the rename A -> D. If the original procedure makes no false rejection, the augmented procedure rejects R = R0 + D' with D' = min(D, m - R0) <= D, at most D' of them false; R = 0 gives FDP = 0; otherwise FDP <= D'/(R0 + D') <= D/(R0 + D) because x -> x/(R0 + x) is increasing; and D <= gamma R0/(1 - gamma) iff D (1 - gamma) <= gamma R0 iff D <= gamma (R0 + D), so FDP <= gamma. Hence {FDP > gamma} needs a false rejection by the original procedure: probability <= alpha. Correct, and the letters D, D' no longer clash with the active set A.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html s9 bullet 'The studentizing scale is wrong under serial correlation' (line 878); Problem E2 (a)-(c), lines 1027-1075
rows.evidence: unchanged since 8352c53 (git diff checked); round-14 evidence: Re-derived at 45559ab (the passage around (c) changed). For d_t = phi d_{t-1} + e_t with iid e of variance s^2: the marginal variance is s^2/(1-phi^2); the long-run variance (sum of autocovariances, gamma_h = phi^|h| s^2/(1-phi^2)) is s^2/(1-phi)^2, so T Var(dbar) -> s^2/(1-phi)^2. The iid-studentized t = dbar/(sd/sqrt(T)) therefore has limiting variance [s^2/(1-phi)^2] / [s^2/(1-phi^2)] = (1+phi)/(1-phi) = 1.857 at phi = 0.3 (sd 1.363), as E2(a) and the line-878 bullet say. A single-date bootstrap resamples as if iid, so t* is approximately N(0,1) and its 95% quantile is about 1.645; the test rejects when t > 1.645, with probability P(N(0, 1.857) > 1.645) = 0.1137 (E2(b)). Longer blocks restore the serial dependence in t*, so t* inherits the variance 1.857 and the critical value rises: 0.113 / 0.063 / 0.067 in the snippet (exact rerun), 0.11 / 0.05 / 0.09 in my independent loop version (L05-num-E2). The bullet's claim that the stationary bootstrap 'reproduces the same distortion in t*' is the same fact; nothing in it changed. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L06.html lines 274-277 (proof of Proposition 4.3)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 8352c53 (git diff checked); round-14 evidence: Re-derived step by step. (1) Lemma 2.2's lower Mills bound x phi(x)/(1+x^2) ≤ Q(x) gives phi(z) ≤ Q(z)(z+1/z); with e^{−z²/2} = sqrt(2 pi) phi(z) and p = 2Q(z): e^{−z²/2} ≤ sqrt(pi/2) p (z+1/z). (2) It suffices that −e p ln p ≥ sqrt(pi/2) p (z+1/z), i.e. u(z) = −ln p − c(z+1/z) ≥ 0 with c = sqrt(pi/2)/e. (3) u'(z) = phi/Q − c(1−1/z²) (d/dz of −ln p = phi/Q); phi/Q ≥ z (upper Mills bound, 0 violations on the grid) and z > c(1−1/z²) for z > 0 (c < 1), so u' > 0 (grid minimum 1.52). (4) At p = 1/e: z* = 0.900453 and u(z*) = 1 − c(z*+1/z*) = 0.072789 > 0. (5) p ≤ 1/e means z ≥ z*, so u(z) ≥ u(z*) > 0. (6) The MBF minimality (Theorem 4.2) gives the last sentence. All steps re-derived and the numbers checked in out_num_prop43.txt. PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html line 598 (new T span: 'In this design the Simes inequality also follows from Lesson 3 alone'); Lesson 3 Definition 5.1, Theorem 5.2, Proposition 5.3 (course/modules/S/S7/L03.html lines 262-282); Theorem 7.5 (L05.html lines 559-571)
rows.evidence: Derivation, written out and checked: (1) Lab 5's true-null statistics are z_j = sqrt(rho) W + sqrt(1-rho) eps_j with mu_j = 0 (the lab code: z = sqrt(rho) w + sqrt(1-rho) e + mu), p_j = 1 - Phi(z_j), rho in [0,1): this is Proposition 5.3's model restricted to the nulls, so the true-null p-values are PRDS on every subset (Definition 5.1). (2) Theorem 5.2's hypotheses hold for the family of the m0 true-null p-values (the family is all true nulls, so PRDS on the true nulls is PRDS on the family; each p_j is super-uniform because z_j ~ N(0,1) gives p_j ~ U(0,1); P(p_j <= u) = u > 0 for u > 0). Its bound FDR <= m0' q / m' with m' = m0' = m0 gives FDR <= q = alpha for BH at level alpha on the family. (3) When every hypothesis in the family is true, V = R, so FDR = E[1{R >= 1}] = P(R >= 1). (4) BH at level alpha on m0 p-values (step-up) rejects at least one hypothesis iff q_(l) <= l alpha/m0 for some l <= m0. Hence P(union_{l<=m0} {q_(l) <= l alpha/m0}) <= alpha: the Simes inequality for the true-null p-values. (5) Theorem 7.5 (containment {FDP > gamma} subset of union_{l<=M}{q_(l) <= l alpha/m0}, M <= m0, for the step-down with constants (3)) gives P(FDP > gamma) <= alpha for every rho in [0,1). Numerical check (num/simes_mtp2_check.py, seeded; output num/simes_mtp2_check.out): union frequency for m0 = 20, 100, 450 and rho = 0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 0.95 is between 0.0163 and 0.0508 (the largest, 0.0508 +- 0.0011 at m0 = 450, rho = 0, is the independent case where the Simes bound is exact at alpha; the difference from 0.05 is 0.7 se); BH any-rejection and the Simes union agree on the same draws (0.036 and 0.036, rho 0.5, m0 30). The paragraph's sentences are correct as written. Grade T: proved on the page from Lesson 3's proved results. The span carries no data-cite, as for the other proofs on the page (rows L05-math-thm31, L05-grade-remark65).
